test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: According to sympatric speciation, the rising of a new species occurs when:

options.text: one species is separated into different groups due to geologic events like mountain formation
organisms from the same species start to show different behavioural characteristics
two groups of the same species cannot interbreed among themselves despite living in the same geographic location
the two groups of organisms from the same species would phenotypically look different

solution:
The correct answer is __**two groups of the same species cannot interbreed among themselves despite living in the same geographic location**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sympatric speciation occurs without geographic isolation; species evolve from a single ancestral species while inhabiting the same geographic region.
 
• It typically involves reproductive isolation due to genetic, behavioral, or ecological differences preventing interbreeding.
 
• This form of speciation can be driven by factors such as polyploidy, sexual selection, and ecological niche differentiation.
 
• Examples include the divergence of cichlid fish in African lakes and apple maggot flies in North America.
 
• Sympatric speciation emphasizes the role of intrinsic factors within the population rather than external barriers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reproductive Isolation**

 
 
• A key mechanism in speciation, preventing different species from interbreeding.
 
• Includes prezygotic barriers (e.g., temporal isolation) and postzygotic barriers (e.g., hybrid sterility).
 
 
 
• **Polyploidy**
 
 
• Occurs when an organism has more than two complete sets of chromosomes.
 
• Common in plants and can lead to instant speciation.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Niche Differentiation**
 
 
• Different populations exploit different resources or habitats.
 
• Can lead to divergence in traits and reproductive isolation.
 
 
 
• **Sexual Selection**
 
 
• Mates are chosen based on specific traits, leading to reproductive isolation.
 
• Can drive rapid evolution and speciation.
